patient.chief_complaint: Acute bilateral leg weakness and inability to walk — 3 days
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. E is a 52-year-old financial consultant with a history of stage IIA breast cancer (ER+, treated with lumpectomy, radiation, and adjuvant letrozole) who presents with 3-day history of acute bilateral leg weakness and inability to ambulate. She was scheduled for a breast cancer surveillance mammogram 3 weeks ago, which showed a suspicious area requiring biopsy; results are pending and she is in a state of extreme anxiety about possible cancer recurrence. Her bilateral leg weakness developed acutely over the course of a single day, beginning with heaviness and progressing to inability to bear weight. She has no back pain, no bowel or bladder dysfunction, and no saddle anesthesia. She denies any headache, neck stiffness, or visual changes. She has no fever. She is extremely worried about spinal cord compression from breast cancer metastasis. Her oncologist has been alerted and has requested urgent neurological evaluation. The diagnostic challenge is that: (1) spinal cord compression from breast cancer is a real and serious possibility that requires urgent exclusion, and (2) FND is the more likely diagnosis given positive functional signs and identified cancer anxiety precipitant.

results.title: Cancer-related fear and somatization in breast cancer survivors

output.summary: Cancer recurrence fear is a major psychological burden in breast cancer survivors and is a recognised precipitant of functional neurological disorder and somatic symptom disorder in this population. Pending diagnostic procedures create a specific acute anxiety state that has been associated with somatic symptom exacerbation in published cohort studies. Psychological interventions targeting health anxiety and cancer-specific fears have demonstrated efficacy in randomised trials for breast cancer survivors. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Functional neurological disorder — bilateral functional paraparesis, in breast cancer survivor with cancer recurrence anxiety (spinal cord compression excluded)

differential.diagnosis: Epidural spinal cord compression (breast cancer metastasis)
differential.key_features: Full spine MRI with contrast: no epidural mass, no vertebral metastases, no cord compression. Normal ALP and calcium. Normal tumor markers.
Normal CSF cytology with negative CK7 immunostain; no leptomeningeal enhancement on MRI
Anti-amphiphysin negative (most common breast cancer paraneoplastic antibody); normal NCS

Normal spinal cord signal on MRI — no T2 cord changes; radiation myelopathy typically develops 6-24 months after radiation (her radiation was 4 years ago at this point, delayed onset possible but no cord lesion on MRI)

optimal_actions.action: Full spine MRI with contrast (URGENT) — exclude spinal cord compression
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal — no metastases, no cord compression

optimal_actions.action: Brain MRI with contrast — exclude brain metastases
CSF with cytology and breast cancer immunostain — exclude leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
Paraneoplastic panel (especially anti-amphiphysin for breast cancer)
FND sign assessment and psychiatric evaluation for cancer anxiety
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Positive Hoover sign; severe health anxiety; pending biopsy precipitant

critical_actions: Full spine MRI with contrast — URGENT, spinal cord compression is a true emergency
Do not delay cancer workup even if positive FND signs are present — both can coexist
contraindicated_actions: Diagnosing FND without excluding spinal cord compression by imaging — potentially life-altering error
Delaying imaging for positive functional signs alone — cancer history requires urgent organic exclusion
key_reasoning_points: Breast cancer history changes the diagnostic algorithm: bilateral leg weakness requires URGENT full spine MRI to exclude epidural cord compression — this is a true neurological emergency if missed
Normal spine MRI AND normal CSF cytology together essentially exclude both cord compression and leptomeningeal carcinomatosis
Anti-amphiphysin is the most important paraneoplastic antibody in breast cancer — it causes a stiff-person-like syndrome and motor neuron disease; negative result excludes this
Pending biopsy results creating cancer recurrence anxiety is the identified precipitant — expediting the biopsy result and oncology communication is part of the treatment

red_herrings.data_point: Breast cancer history and bilateral leg weakness

red_herrings.intended_effect: Focus exclusively on cancer-related workup and miss positive FND signs
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Cancer workup is mandatory AND FND assessment (positive Hoover signs) should be performed in parallel — normal spine MRI and CSF combined with positive functional signs confirm FND
